title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a smooth proper connected complex curve of genus g ≥ 2. Grothendieck constructs the canonical flat PGL(2)-torsor coming from Fuchsian uniformization. In his notation G' = GP(1) = PGL(2).

(1) Construction. For each point x of X, take the universal cover X̃(x) based at x, with base point x̃. By uniformization it is isomorphic to the Poincaré disc D. The set Iso(D_0, (X̃(x), x̃)) is a right torsor under Aut_an(D_0) ≅ PSU(1,1) ≅ PSL(2,R) = G'_R. Extending structure group along G'_R ⊂ G'_C gives a G'_C-torsor P_x.

(2) Global structure. As x varies, the P_x are the fibres of a principal bundle with flat structure, namely the one associated to the monodromy representation π1(X) → G'_R ⊂ G'_C. This is the holonomy of the hyperbolic structure. Equivalently it is the flat P^1-bundle X̃ ×_π P^1, carrying the developing-map section.

(3) Side remark. For each x there is a unique holomorphic embedding of X̃(x) into T_x(X) whose image is a disc and whose tangent map at x̃ is the identity. This is the normalised Riemann map; the radius of the disc is fixed by the hyperbolic metric at x.

(4) Dependence on base point. He records how the torsors depend on the base point: P(x, ρq) = P(x, q) ∧^{G'_C}_{int(ρ)}. He also lists real and complex forms with a maximal-torus-like subgroup S ⊂ G', and the inclusion C* ⊂ GL(2,R) ⊂ GL(2,C).

(5) Algebraic question. He asks for the algebraic avatar of this object:
- a) an invertible sheaf, Ω^{-1} (the tangent bundle, i.e. the normal bundle of the developing section, the 'G_m → GP' piece);
- b) the bundle P(Ω^{-1} ⊕ Ω) with integrable connection.
The boxed problem reads: find a canonical algebraic integrable connection on P(Ω^{-1}+Ω) = V(Ω^2). He starts to compute connection matrices: Hom(Ω^{-1}⊕Ω, (Ω^{-1}⊕Ω)⊗Ω) has entries such as Ω^3 and Ω, and (Ω^{-1}⊕Ω)⊗Ω = O + Ω^2. The pair (D, ω) is matched with (ϖ, Δ).

(6) Context from the neighbouring pages.
- The previous page computes 1 → μ2 → SL2 → PGL2 → 1, the relation c'_2 = ½c_2, SO(2), and the principal-parts sequences P^n_{X/k}.
- The next page computes Euler classes: E' = ½E, the Euler class 2g−2 of the Fuchsian representation, g−1 after halving, and the μ2 obstruction in H^2(X, Z/2) to lifting to SL2 (theta characteristics).

In modern terms, this page is the uniformizing projective structure / indigenous bundle / PGL2-oper of a hyperbolic curve. The question is whether it can be made algebraic and canonical.
errors: P(Ω^{-1}⊕Ω) (≅ P(O⊕Ω^2)) is not the holomorphic P^1-bundle underlying the uniformization torsor. That bundle is P of the non-split extension 0→Ω^{1/2}→E→Ω^{-1/2}→0 (Gunning's indigenous bundle), equivalently P(J^1(T_X)). The developing section has normal bundle T_X = Ω^{-1}, so the degree difference must be 2g−2, not 4g−4.

As posed, the boxed problem has no solution. By Weil–Atiyah, a decomposable rank-2 bundle whose summands have nonzero degree admits no holomorphic connection. More generally, P(L1⊕L2) with deg L1 ≠ deg L2 carries no holomorphic projective connection. Equivalently, the oper (transversality) condition needs the second fundamental form to be an isomorphism, which forces ratio Ω, not Ω^2.

Even with the correct bundle, holomorphic connections of oper type form an affine space over H^0(Ω^{⊗2}). There is no canonical algebraic choice: the uniformizing one is transcendental. So 'canonique (alg)' cannot be achieved over C, though it becomes meaningful p-adically or in characteristic p.
Minor: Aut_an(D_0) is the real form G'_R = PSL(2,R); the transcription/scan seems to write G'_C before extending structure group.

ideas.what: Canonical flat PGL2-torsor on a hyperbolic curve built from pointed universal covers, Iso(D, (X̃(x), x̃)), extended from PSL2(R) to PGL2(C)
ideas.modern_name: Uniformizing projective structure / Fuchsian holonomy / uniformization oper

ideas.what: Unique holomorphic embedding of the pointed universal cover into T_x X with disc image and identity differential
Seek a canonical algebraic integrable connection on the P^1-bundle attached to Ω (the algebraic shadow of uniformization)
ideas.modern_name: Indigenous bundles / opers; canonical (Frobenius-compatible) indigenous bundles in p-adic Teichmüller theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning; Ihara (Schwarzian equations in char p, 1970s); Mochizuki (p-adic Teichmüller theory, 1990s)

ideas.what: Euler class bookkeeping E' = ½E, 2g−2 versus g−1, μ2 obstruction to lifting to SL2 (adjacent pages)
ideas.modern_name: Milnor–Wood equality for Fuchsian representations; spin lifts / theta characteristics

missed.claim: In a folder on the divided-power de Rham complex (crystalline context, c. 1976), Grothendieck asks for a canonical *algebraic* integrable connection on the P^1-bundle built from Ω^{±1} that algebraizes Fuchsian uniformization. Over C this cannot be canonical. The natural home of the question is characteristic p / p-adic, where canonical Frobenius-compatible indigenous bundles exist (Mochizuki's p-adic Teichmüller theory, prefigured by Ihara). The page links uniformization with the crystalline/PD de Rham programme well before that theory, though only as a question with a mis-specified bundle.
missed.quote: Trouver une connexion intégrable (alg) canonique sur P(Ω^{-1}+Ω) = V(Ω^2)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical evidence that Grothendieck considered algebraizing the uniformizing oper in a crystalline setting, relevant to the genealogy of p-adic Teichmüller theory and anabelian geometry. It is not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is classical (uniformization, indigenous bundles, Euler class of Fuchsian representations), and the algebraic formulation uses the wrong bundle. Mildly interesting historically: Grothendieck poses the algebraic-canonical-oper question inside crystalline notes, anticipating themes later developed by Ihara and Mochizuki.
transcription_corrections: 'Autan(D_0)' should read Aut_an(D_0) (analytic automorphisms of the disc). After the struck text, the group should be G'_R = PSL(2,R), extended afterwards to G'_C.
'rev. universel de X en x' — the pointed universal cover (X̃(x), x̃) is meant.
'fibré principal tordu [?]' — the insertion over the struck text is probably 'tors.' (torseur), i.e. a principal bundle with flat structure.
'S'_C ⊂ G' ⊂ G'_C' in the margin likely reads '∀ρ ∈ S'_C, G' ⊂ G'_C' (ρ is the element used in int(ρ)).
